blocks.text: Nimble in 2026: what you get

Nimble (Nimbleway) is an AI-first web-data platform. It offers residential proxies with fast response times and unlimited concurrency, but most of its product investment goes into the Nimble Browser, SERP and e-commerce APIs, and data-services plans that start in the thousands of dollars per month. It does not disclose its residential pool size, and its per-GB rates are among the highest here, so it competes on finished results rather than cheap traffic.

Strengths: Strong managed APIs and an AI-driven browser; Unlimited concurrency on proxies; Credits shared across all Nimble products; Free 5,000-page API trial. Weak spots: No published pool size; HTTP/HTTPS only, no SOCKS5 on proxies; High per-GB price for raw residential traffic.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap has sold proxies since 2018 and says it serves 45,000+ customers. It offers seven product types: static residential (ISP) in IPv4 and IPv6, rotating residential, datacenter IPv4 and IPv6, and static and rotating mobile. Rotating residential is pure pay-as-you-go with no monthly plan, and the site claims coverage in 180+ countries. Targeting is mainly country and ISP level, and all products support SOCKS5 including UDP. It is a strong value pick, though independent benchmarks of its rotating pool have been mixed.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: Nimble vs Proxy-Cheap

Nimble's plan cards list residential proxy traffic at $8/GB pay-as-you-go, falling through credit packages ($150 and $600 entry packages) toward $5.30/GB; its current developer documentation lists $5.30/GB for residential traffic without a commitment. Annual billing saves 15%. Its scraping APIs bill $0.90 to $1.45 per 1,000 URLs depending on rendering.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

For a 10 GB month, Proxy-Cheap costs about $7.80 while Nimble costs about $53, so Proxy-Cheap saves around 85%. For a 100 GB month, Proxy-Cheap costs about $78 while Nimble costs about $530, so Proxy-Cheap saves around 85%. Both Nimble and Proxy-Cheap work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Nimble and Proxy-Cheap do not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. Nimble lists 'Not published' and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Nimble lists Worldwide countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, Nimble offers country, state and city, while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Protocol support is a real difference here. Proxy-Cheap supports HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5 (TCP and UDP), while Nimble offers HTTP, HTTPS. If your tooling needs SOCKS5, for example some anti-detect browsers, desktop apps or non-HTTP traffic, that settles it in Proxy-Cheap's favour. On sessions, Nimble offers auto-rotation by default; sticky sessions available, and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Nimble wins. The deciding factor for Nimble: its managed APIs remove much of the anti-bot work. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed.
SERP and rank tracking: Nimble. Nimble has the edge here. Why: its SERP API and search agents return structured results. How Proxy-Cheap compares: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost.

Social media and multi-account management: Proxy-Cheap wins. The deciding factor for Proxy-Cheap: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities. The limitation on the Nimble side: no SOCKS5 and a high per-GB cost make it a poor fit for account work.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Nimble wins. The deciding factor for Nimble: dedicated e-commerce data APIs. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: fine for country-level price checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Nimble. Nimble has the edge here. Why: good geo targeting but no published pool data. How Proxy-Cheap compares: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential.
Tight budgets: Proxy-Cheap wins. The deciding factor for Proxy-Cheap: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. The limitation on the Nimble side: per-GB rates are among the highest here.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Nimble: Free trial of 5,000 web pages on its APIs. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. Nimble: Sales-led onboarding for data-services plans. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Nimble and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle Nimble vs Proxy-Cheap faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Nimble: free trial of 5,000 web pages on its APIs; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs).

2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day. 3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Nimble comes out ahead in 4, Proxy-Cheap in 2, and 0 are ties. That makes Nimble the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Nimble is strongest for teams that want structured data rather than raw IPs, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
